Plot a lag transition network

Source: R/plot-transitions.R
plot_transitions.Rd

plot_transitions() draws a lag transition network with cograph: the states are nodes and the transitions between them directed edges. Which quantity weights the edges decides what the network shows. Weighted by adjusted residuals it is a residual network: edges show where a transition is more frequent (over-represented) or less frequent (avoided) than independence predicts, the reading of lag sequential analysis. Weighted by transition probabilities it is the network of Transition Network Analysis, which shows where the process goes next, whether or not that is more than chance.

With weights = "residuals" (default), over-represented transitions are solid blue edges and avoided transitions dashed red edges; "yules_q" draws the same signed network on the bounded Yule's Q scale, and "lift" the ratio of observed to expected counts. With "prob" (or its aliases "tna" and "relative") or "count", the network is drawn in the style of Transition Network Analysis, each node ringed by its initial-state probability; probability edges below 0.05 are hidden unless edge_cutoff is passed. Dense networks are thinned with significant or, better at large sample sizes where nearly every cell is significant, with top.

The same display is plot(fit, type = "network"). For the full table use the residual heatmap of plot.lsa(); for the per-source breakdown, plot_chords() or plot_polar().

Usage

plot_transitions(
  fit,
  weights = c("residuals", "tna", "relative", "count", "prob", "lift", "yules_q"),
  significant = FALSE,
  top = NULL,
  decimals = 1,
  node_fill = "white",
  edge_labels = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

An lsa fit from lsa().

weights

Edge weight: "residuals" (default), "tna", "relative", "prob" (the three are the transition probability), "count", "lift" or "yules_q".

significant

Keep only transitions whose residual p-value is below the fit's alpha (default FALSE).

top

Keep only the strongest edges by absolute weight: a fraction below 1 keeps that share of the edges, a number of 1 or more keeps that many. Default NULL (all edges). Applied after significant.

decimals

Decimal places of the edge labels (default 1).

node_fill

Node colour (default "white"). The probability and count networks colour nodes by state unless node_fill is set.

edge_labels

Show the edge weights as labels (default TRUE).

...

Passed to cograph::splot(), for example layout, node_shape, edge_cutoff or curvature.

Value

The network drawn by cograph::splot(), invisibly; the plot is drawn on the current device.

See also

plot.lsa(), plot_chords(), transitions(), transition_probabilities()

Examples

fit <- lsa(engagement)
plot_transitions(fit)

plot_transitions(fit, weights = "prob")


fit9 <- lsa(group_regulation)
plot_transitions(fit9, top = 12)

plot_transitions(fit9, weights = "yules_q", significant = TRUE)
